summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analysing the confidential data drops, then building a product (poller, extraction/recheck agents, supplier communication, approver UI) and polishing it before the hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's launch plan hides real shortfalls (overbooked 80,000 art-book receipt, 5,600 failed statues, late game cards) and built the Lighthouse product with a versioned poller, agents, decision UI, Routines page and a 'How we got here' case flow. Many UI fixes are committed on `main` (about 19 commits ahead of origin, unpushed); the hand-in has moved to 12:45 and the last 'show 1 only with more options' tweak was still in progress.

repo: The portal API has only three endpoints (list files, get file, archive.zip) and no webhooks or change feed. Detecting drops means polling the file list and comparing SHA-256, because files are replaced under the same name.
Data in `data/`, `.env` and scans must stay gitignored because it is confidential. `.env.example` is committed with an empty token.
Team workflow lives in `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRESS.md`; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in `PROGRESS.md`.

Routine steps like 'Chase once if no answer' and 'Ask for a status' are valid only for certain watched kinds (waiting messages, shipments). The server rejects them elsewhere with 'step N cannot be done on open decisions'.
The API does not load `.env` on import. Settings such as `ASK_VIEWER_TITLE` must be read through a helper that loads `.env` first or they are missing after restart.
Number keys 1-9 only choose an option; ⌘↵ carries out the chosen one. Option 1 is the recommendation and is pre-selected, so a '1' badge is redundant unless more options are shown.
The routine diagram's connector and node components are exported from `FlowGraph.tsx` and reused by `CaseFlow.tsx`, so the two views stay visually consistent.
Routines code calls Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) with the key from `.env`, independent of `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER`.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' flow built from each case's own data (agent steps, evidence, prediction, approval rule, options); missing steps are omitted, never invented. Reuses the connector and box from FlowGraph.tsx. Full view is the default, with a compact 'Less' mode.

workflow: The Entire hooks only checkpoint when repo files change; a session that only reads files logs 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint', which is not a failure.
Subagents worked well for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and for drawing logo variants without touching the repo.
Experimental UI work goes on separate branches with desktop and phone screenshots before merging. A premature merge of the chat UI had to be undone because it misread what the team wanted.
Checking the interview notes and team memory before building would have avoided building the wrong Pulse feature (a chat instead of the flow view).
The user's deadline changed (12:00 to 12:45) without the assistant knowing, so deadline reminders were wrong for a while.

friction: The portal token was empty at the start, which blocked any data work until the user supplied it.
The assistant misread what the team liked in Pulse and built a duplicate chat UI with mismatched colours, then had to revert the merge.
The first two-column snake layout of the case flow read right to left and confused the user; it was replaced by a single column.

The flow's compact and full views went through several iterations (phone empty gaps, 'Details' looking identical, page auto-scrolling on load) and an edit was interrupted mid-way, leaving unclear uncommitted state.
The top bar was crowded after adding the role chip and status; it needed a three-column grid and the heartbeat moved.
'Chase once if no answer' appeared to be broken but was only invalid for the routine kind; the menu offered it everywhere.
The 'Ask Maren to approve' button jumping could not be reproduced.
Whether portal data is identical across teams and whether sent emails create portal files is undocumented.
open_items: `main` is about 19 commits ahead of origin and unpushed, and live was not restarted; it must be pushed before the hand-in at 12:45.
Show the '1' key badge only when more options are visible; this was in progress when the transcript ended.
The parked branch `jonas/pulse-ui` (Describe it chat) is not merged and is probably not wanted.
The Routines page is a long wall when there are many routines; the plan is a compact list with details on demand, a ⋯ menu and duplicate detection, to be done after the hand-in.
The 'send the email, then chase once if no answer' routine needs a follow-up watcher on the sent message.
Pick and apply a Lighthouse logo variant (the assistant prefers 3, the subagent 2) to the favicon, top bar and sign-in page.
Make 'N decisions' in the top bar open a bottom-sheet case list on phones (about 15 minutes, optional).
Send the Karton Nowak art-book order and the Boise terms reply, which require a registered sender address in the portal Settings and an inbox. The Nowak offer was valid for 24 hours.
The briefing page and doc still show the 14:00 state and do not include the 14:37 drop; the earlier Claude doc may need deleting.
Rotate the portal password, which was pasted into Discord.
Code in the case-flow branch was not tested in a browser by clicking 'Details'; the compact view was not re-screenshotted after the shorter connectors.
